# Overview

`Edge_Network()` performs miRNA gene interaction (MGI) enrichment
analysis through network propagation. It builds a combined MGI and GGI
network, converts it to its line graph so that edges become nodes, and
runs a random walk with restart seeded from the differentially expressed
MGIs. Each pathway is scored by how much of the propagated signal lands
on its own MGIs, with significance assessed against permuted restart
sets, controlled by `iter`. It needs a gene-gene interaction (GGI) network
in addition to `background_MGI`.
Because the line graph scales with the combined size of the background
MGI and GGI networks, this method can be memory and time intensive on
real sized data. Consider increasing `ncores` for large analyses.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a three column data frame with columns `pathway`, `miRNA`,
  and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `gene_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `gene`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `mir_mat` and `gene_mat`, raw expression matrices with samples as
  columns.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).
* `GGI_source` or `background_GGI`, selecting the gene to gene
  interaction network (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 1, for details on
  `background_GGI` and `GGI_source`).
* `iter`, the number of permuted restart sets. The function default is
  1000. This vignette uses `iter = 10` to keep build time short on the
  small toy dataset.
* `seed`, an optional integer for reproducible permutation draws.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_mat)
data(toy_mir_mat)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run Edge-Network

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "Edge_Network",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI,
    GGI_source = "Reactome",
    gene_mat = toy_gene_mat,
    mir_mat = toy_mir_mat
)
```

`input_data$data$Edge_Network` holds the differentially expressed MGIs.
`input_data$pathway$TG`, `input_data$pathway$Edge`, and
`input_data$pathway_GGI` hold the pathway gene, MGI, and GGI sets.
`input_data$MGI` and `input_data$GGI` hold the background MGI and GGI
networks restricted to the genes and miRNAs relevant to `toy_pathway` and
`toy_mir_DEdata`/`toy_gene_DEdata`.

```{r run-edge-network}
res <- Edge_Network(
    DEMGI = input_data$data$Edge_Network,
    pathway_gene = input_data$pathway$TG,
    pathway_MGI = input_data$pathway$Edge,
    pathway_GGI = input_data$pathway_GGI,
    MGI = input_data$MGI,
    GGI = input_data$GGI,
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000,
    iter = 10,
    ncores = 1,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    seed = 42
)
res_display <- head(res)
res_display$contribute_edge <- NULL
res_display
```

`contribute_edge` is omitted from the display above because it lists every
contributing edge for a pathway as a single string, which can be very long
on the toy network and is better inspected directly on `res` than printed
in full here. `n_contribute_edge` reports how many edges that string holds.

# Run through miREA()

`Edge_Network()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is
useful when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a
single `miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). `Edge_Network()` itself has no `background` argument,
it uses `input_data$MGI`/`input_data$GGI` directly instead, but `miREA()`
still requires a `background` for the `Edge` target, since
`Edge_ORA()`/`Edge_Score2D()`/`Edge_Topology()` share that target and do
use it. For a single target, `background` can be a plain character
vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
background <- unique(paste0(background_MGI$miRNA, ":", background_MGI$gene))
result <- miREA(
    methods = "Edge_Network",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = background,
    minSize = 2,
    maxSize = 5000,
    iter = 10,
    ncores = 1,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    seed = 42
)
result_display <- head(result$result$Edge_Network)
result_display$contribute_edge <- NULL
result_display
```
